title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part 2 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (cote 140-3). Grothendieck is building auxiliary algebraic groups attached to a group G. G is presumably GL_2-like, with SG = Ker det, PG = G/centre, and centre ≅ G_m. The data are two 'sections' ρ, σ of G, apparently the order-2 and order-3 type elements relevant to the loop equations. Attached to them are T_ρ (a torus) with a character δ_ρ: T_ρ → G_m, and N'_σ (a normaliser-type group) with a character δ_σ: N'_σ → G_m and a sign ε_σ: N'_σ → μ_2.

On the previous page he built T_{ρ,σ}, its characters χ and (ε_3, ε_2), and a group R_{ρ,σ} sitting in an extension 1 → μ_2 → R_{ρ,σ} → T_{ρ,σ} → 1. That extension is the pullback of the squaring map G_m → G_m along χ.

This page makes T_{ρ,σ} explicit as a subgroup of T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, where δ_0: T_0 ≅ G_m:
T_{ρ,σ} = {(u, a, b) | δ_0(u) = δ_σ(b) = ε' δ_ρ(a), ε'^2 = 1}.
Since δ_0 is an isomorphism, u is determined by b. So
T_{ρ,σ} ≅ {(a, b) ∈ T_ρ × N'_σ | δ_ρ(a) = ± δ_σ(b)},
the fibre product of T_ρ and N'_σ over G_m/μ_2.

The characters are (110):
- χ(a, b) = δ_σ(b);
- ε_3(a, b) = δ_ρ(a)/δ_σ(b), which lies in μ_2;
- ε_1(a, b) = ε_σ(b).

With this, the 'universal' group M_{ρ,σ} is defined via (102). From the description (114), it is a quotient of R_{ρ,σ} × SG, i.e. an amalgamated or central product of R_{ρ,σ} and SG. It carries a homomorphism Θ: M_{ρ,σ} → G, induced on quotients by:
- the inclusion SG ⊂ G;
- a map R_{ρ,σ} → G, compatible with κ: R_{ρ,σ} → G_m ≅ Centre(G) ⊂ G.

Composites (113):
- Θ̃: M → G → PG;
- χ = det ∘ Θ: M → G_m.

Exact sequence (114): 1 → SG → M_{ρ,σ} → T_{ρ,σ} → 1, with T_{ρ,σ} ≅ R_{ρ,σ}/μ_2.

Purpose: the next page makes it explicit. The 'coarse' structure of M_{ρ,σ} does not depend on the actual sections ρ, σ, only on their existence. Finer structure, namely the n-sections M_{ρ,σ}(n), does depend on them and might allow ρ, σ to be recovered. All of this is part of the group-theoretic bookkeeping (the cube diagrams (95)/(96)) for solutions of the loop equations in a linear group. The construction is elementary: fibre products of tori and normalisers over G_m, and central products.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. There are two consistency points. First, ε_3 = δ_ρ(a)/δ_σ(b) is ±1 by the defining condition, so it is indeed μ_2-valued. Second, χ is defined both on T_{ρ,σ} as δ_σ(b) and on M as det∘Θ; these agree only after identifying via (114), which is asserted rather than checked.
On the previous page the μ_2-valued characters are (ε_3, ε_2), but here (110) lists ε_3 and ε_1. This is either a renumbering or a slip in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Description of T_{ρ,σ} as the fibre product of a torus T_ρ and a normaliser N'_σ over G_m modulo ±1, i.e. pairs with δ_ρ(a) = ±δ_σ(b).
ideas.modern_name: fibre product / central product of diagonalisable and normaliser group schemes

ideas.what: Group M_{ρ,σ}, an extension of T_{ρ,σ} by SG with a homomorphism Θ to G, built as a quotient of R_{ρ,σ} × SG; composites with G → PG and det.
ideas.modern_name: central product / extension of algebraic groups by the derived group SL

ideas.what: Overall programme: algebraic groups attached to loop-equation solutions in linear groups (from the 'équation des lacets' / GT setting).
ideas.modern_name: representations of Teichmüller-tower / GT relations in GL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); later Drinfeld, Ihara for GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the lacets equations only in general terms

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine bookkeeping of fibre products and extensions of algebraic groups within a larger unpublished computation. It contains no standalone result or new connection.
transcription_corrections: In (114) the final isomorphism should read T_{ρ,σ} ≅ R_{ρ,σ}/μ_2 (consistent with (106)), not /μ_n.
In (109) the condition reads δ_0(u) = δ_σ(b) = ε'δ_ρ(a); in the second form, δ_ρ(a) = ε'δ_σ(b) with a ∈ T_ρ, b ∈ N'_σ.
Line after (110): 'À l'aide de ceci, on peut construire M_{ρ,σ} par (102), et bien entendu l'homo[morphisme]'.
